source.title: Artificial Neural Networks: A Way to Find Well-Generalizing, High-Entropy Sharp Minima
source.authors: Enzo Tartaglione; Andrea Bragagnolo; Marco Grangetto

record.tranche_reason: The study compares generalization with Hessian-based sharpness and reports a well-generalizing narrow minimum, qualifying the broad idea that sharper minima generalize worse. It does not test the claim versions’ specific interventions or magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports pruning and reinitialization results, but those do not test V1–V6 or V8. Results comparing sharpness and generalization, and PSP measurements compared across solutions with different generalization, bear on the claim’s subject but do not measure V7’s magnitude-scaled perturbation criterion.
record.test_reason: The study compares pruning strategies and relates their performance to Hessian eigenvalues and PSP statistics. It does not test any supplied version: Hessian curvature is not V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation measure, and the study does not evaluate its ranking of generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures. The record's T5 classification is therefore unwarranted.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that gradual pruning reaches greater sparsity and can find well-generalizing sharp minima inaccessible to the compared one-shot approaches. They report lower PSP norms and higher second-order PSP entropy, interpreting the latter as less class-specific features. Transfer-learning benefits and concerns about second-order optimization are proposed implications, not tested outcomes.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares gradual LOBSTER pruning with one-shot pruning and reinitialization, rather than testing the claim versions’ methods. It uses SGD with standard hyper-parameters and data augmentation; the sharpness analysis uses top-5 Hessian eigenvalues rather than magnitude-scaled weight perturbations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported pruning and reinitialization performance varies with architecture, dataset and compression rate; LeNet-5 on MNIST retains accuracy at high compression, while Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 settings degrade at lower compression. The detailed sharpness and PSP comparisons are for LeNet-5 on MNIST at 99.57% pruning.

fits_no_version.finding: At 99.57% parameter pruning, gradually pruned LeNet-5 on MNIST generalizes slightly better than the best one-shot solution despite having a narrower minimum measured by Hessian eigenvalues.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradual pruning can find solutions with better test performance and greater Hessian curvature than one-shot retraining.

fits_no_version.finding: The better-generalizing gradual solution has lower average PSP L2 norm, comparable first-order PSP entropy, and higher second-order PSP entropy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PSP magnitude and second-order PSP entropy distinguish these pruning solutions, while first-order entropy does not.

record.problems: The detailed sharpness and PSP comparisons focus on one architecture, dataset and compression level. Values for these comparisons are presented in figures and described qualitatively in the text; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The sharpness comparison uses Hessian eigenvalues and does not test the magnitude-aware measure in V7.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results omitted. Figure-only numeric values were not reconstructed; the rows record the paper’s accompanying qualitative descriptions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Widening beyond the width required for zero training error.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers and dependence on tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, and comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The detailed sharpness and PSP evidence concerns LeNet-5 on MNIST at 99.57% pruning. Numerical endpoint values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text. The authors assert broader applicability, but provide these detailed comparisons for this setting.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
The study measures Hessian eigenvalues, not magnitude-scaled weight perturbations; its result does not compare that measure against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: LeNet-5-caffe
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error after gradual pruning and one-shot pruning at the highest compression rate.
rows.baseline: one-shot solution (1-S); numeric baseline not stated
rows.value: gradual solution (G) generalizes slightly better; numeric value figure only
rows.note: The text describes the generalization difference as slight; the plotted test-error values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: The qualitative performance comparison is accurate, but compares pruning methods rather than an intervention named by any version. The slight advantage does not constitute partial evidence for a supplied version. Section 5.2 cites Fig. 1b for test performance; Fig. 2a measures training loss.

rows.subject: LeNet-5-caffe
rows.operation_detail: Compared top-5 Hessian eigenvalues of gradual-pruning and one-shot solutions as a sharpness measure.
rows.measure: Top-5 largest Hessian eigenvalues / minimum width
rows.baseline: one-shot solution (1-S); numeric values not stated
rows.value: gradual solution (G) lies in a narrower minimum; numeric values figure only
rows.note: The paper reports that the gradual solution is narrower despite generalizing slightly better. This is Hessian-based sharpness, not magnitude-scaled perturbation.
rows.check: The reported narrower minimum is supported by the text, but top Hessian eigenvalues do not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance.

rows.subject: LeNet-5-caffe
rows.operation_detail: Compared average L2 norm values of post-synaptic potentials for gradual-pruning and one-shot solutions.
rows.baseline: one-shot solution (1-S); numeric values not stated
rows.value: gradual solution has lower PSP L2-norm values; numeric values figure only
rows.note: The authors state that the solution with better generalization has lower z² values.
rows.check: The lower PSP norm is reported accurately, but PSP magnitude is not a measure named by any supplied version.

rows.subject: LeNet-5-caffe
rows.operation_detail: Compared first-order PSP entropy for gradual-pruning and one-shot solutions.
rows.baseline: one-shot solution (1-S); numeric values not stated
rows.value: gradual and one-shot pruning show comparable first-order entropies; numeric values figure only
rows.note: The paper describes the first-order entropies as comparable.
rows.check: Comparable first-order PSP entropies are reported accurately. Their similarity cannot establish absence of an effect named by any supplied version.

rows.subject: LeNet-5-caffe
rows.operation_detail: Compared second-order PSP entropy for gradual-pruning and one-shot solutions.
rows.baseline: one-shot solution (1-S); numeric values not stated
rows.value: gradual pruning shows higher entropy; numeric values figure only
rows.note: The authors interpret higher entropy in the better-generalizing gradual solution as more general features less specific to a class.
rows.check: Higher second-order PSP entropy is reported accurately, but this statistic does not measure an effect named by any supplied version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
